text:
Predicates:
WorksInStudentJobs(x) ::: x works in student jobs on campus.
NeedsMoneyToPayTuition(x) ::: x needs to earn money to help pay for college tuition.
OrdersTakeoutFrequently(x) ::: x orders takeout frequently in college.
EnjoysDiningHallMealsAndRecipes(x) ::: x enjoys the dining hall meals and recipes.
NotPickyEater(x) ::: x is not a picky eater.
SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x) ::: x spends a lot of their time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
AtSchool(x) ::: x is at Mary's school.
Hannah ::: Hannah (constant representing Hannah).

Premises:
∀x (WorksInStudentJobs(x) → NeedsMoneyToPayTuition(x)) ::: If people at Mary's school work in student jobs, then they need to earn money for tuition.
∀x (OrdersTakeoutFrequently(x) → WorksInStudentJobs(x)) ::: If people order takeout frequently, then they work in student jobs.
∀x (OrdersTakeoutFrequently(x) ∨ (EnjoysDiningHallMealsAndRecipes(x) ∧ ¬PickyEater(x))) ::: People order takeout frequently or enjoy dining hall meals and are not picky eaters.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHallMealsAndRecipes(x) → ¬PickyEater(x)) ::: If they enjoy dining hall meals, then they are not picky eaters.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHallMealsAndRecipes(x) → SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x)) ::: If they enjoy dining hall meals, then they spend a lot of time eating and catching up.
Hannah ∧ WorksInStudentJobs(Hannah) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school and works in student jobs.
(NeedsMoneyToPayTuition(Hannah) → (¬PickyEater(Hannah) ∧ NeedsMoneyToPayTuition(Hannah))) ::: If Hannah needs money to pay tuition, then she is neither a picky eater nor needs to earn money.

Conclusion:
Hannah ∧ (¬PickyEater(Hannah) ∨ (PickyEater(Hannah) → SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(Hannah))) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school and either is not a picky eater or, if she is, then she spends a lot of her time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
